title: Choose the visual world
question: Game Tracker's look: keep the assigned direction, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show the Calendar screen; the real build keeps the same screens and tab bar.

options.label: Release Schedule
options.lineage: The release-schedule pages at the back of a games magazine
options.thesis: Every date set like a magazine's release list: big condensed day numerals, the month as a running header.
materials: cover art as the only full colour
options.viewport: Calendar: the next release's day count set monumental at the top, then a month header rule and each release as a row with a huge day numeral, cover, name, platform and countdown.
options.risk: Can feel like print on a phone if the numerals are timid or the rows too loose.

raised.raise: Blue is reserved for one job: what's next and what's selected.
Exact and vague dates differ by line form (solid vs dashed rule), not by another colour.
The next release's day count is monumental, one message per line.
Hairline rules carry the structure; no boxed cards.
Cover art is the only full colour on screen.

options.label: Strategy Guide
options.lineage: Printed game strategy guides and their checklists
options.thesis: The library read like a guide: chapter tabs per status, completion as a checklist you tick.
options.viewport: Calendar as a guide chapter: numbered section header, releases as a checklist with tick boxes for bell-on games, a coloured tab marking the chapter on the right edge.
options.risk: The most familiar idea for a completion tracker; can tip into gimmick if the tabs get busy.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: Airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: Releases ranked like departures; a moved date stays lit until you've seen it.
options.viewport: Calendar as a board: fixed columns for date, game and status, rows ordered by release, a delayed game's new date held in amber.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: release order and date changes map exactly; loses on gaming identity.
options.risk: Reads as a travel app if the game art is pushed out by the grid.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Rows of cover tiles that grow on focus.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows of covers per month.
options.case: Fails a brand commitment: it is the PS5 home screen's layout.
options.kept: Cover art is the only full colour on screen.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A fixed terrain with one purple course over it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no map in this product, and the palette fights the pinned blue.
options.kept: One colour reserved for the active leg: blue only for what's next.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: State carried by line form on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: Releases as lines on a rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: abstract, and nobody reads release dates as a spectrum.
options.kept: State by line form: solid for exact dates, dashed for vague ones.

options.label: Design Annual
options.thesis: Plates on near-white stock with registration marks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a light print world for a phone used in the dark.
options.kept: Hairline rules carry the structure; no boxed cards.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Yellow bands with one message each and monumental numbers.
options.viewport: The next release as one sign band.
options.case: Fuses poorly: yellow fights the pinned blue and shouts.
options.kept: The next release's number monumental, one message per line.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean iOS-style dark app: grouped lists, system font, blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement an iPhone user expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other tracker by design.
